title: Rabbi Asi, colleague of Rabbi Ami
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: (In the Jerusalem Talmud he is called Rabbi Yasa, Yaysa, or Yisa.) We find an explicit indication that this Rabbi Asi knew Shmuel while he was in Babylonia. Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:8 and Shekalim 2:4 record Rabbi Yisa saying, “While I was still there, I heard Rav Yehudah’s voice asking Shmuel a question.” We likewise find Rabbi Asi reporting in Rav Yehudah’s name in [Bava Metzia 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.43a.3); this was while he was in Babylonia, in his youth. He also reports in the name of Rabbah bar Yirmeyah, a student of Rav and Shmuel. He was younger than Rav Huna: when Rav Huna’s coffin was brought to the Land of Israel, Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi said, “When we were there, we could not raise our heads before him” ([Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.15-16)).

Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:8 relates that when Rabbi Yasa came to the Land of Israel, he wished to bathe in the hot springs of Tiberias. A scoffer encountered him, struck him on the neck, and mockingly remarked that his neck was still soft and needed strengthening. In the end the scoffer was arrested for brigandage and a yoke was placed on his neck. When Rabbi Asi came out of the bathhouse, he encountered the same scoffer and said, “Cursed is your fortune! Is it not written, ‘Now therefore do not scoff, lest your bonds be made strong’?”

[Kiddushin 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.31b.7-9) relates why he went up to the Land of Israel. He had an elderly mother who said, “I want a husband as handsome as you”—she was mentally disturbed. He left her and went to the Land of Israel. Hearing that she was following him, he came before Rabbi Yochanan. Undoubtedly an interval of several years had elapsed: during that time he had studied before Rabbi Chanina and his other teachers before coming to Rabbi Yochanan. The aggadic account, however, tells together the events that occurred in the end. He asked whether he was permitted to leave the Land of Israel; Rabbi Yochanan thought he intended to return to Babylonia and said, “May the Omnipresent bring you back in peace.” He came before Rabbi Elazar and said, “Perhaps Rabbi Yochanan is angry with me.” Meanwhile, after he had left the Land of Israel, he heard that her coffin was coming and said, “Had I known, I would not have left.” [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1 tells](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.3.1.23) the story of Rabbi Yasa hearing that his mother had come to Bostra. He asked Rabbi Yochanan, who replied, “If it is because of danger on the roads, go out; if it is to honor your mother, I do not know,” and so forth.

Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 3:4 likewise says, “When Rabbi Yasa came up here,” and so forth. At the end of Orlah, he told Rabbi Yochanan, “Had I come up to the Land of Israel only to hear this matter, it would have been enough.”

Like his colleague Rabbi Ami, he received teachings from Rabbi Chanina. Thus, Rabbi Asi reports in Rabbi Chanina’s name in [Sanhedrin 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.43b.8) and [Menachot 50b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.50b.16). In [Gittin 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.39b.18), Hyman says that the order should be reversed. Rabbi Asi should be quoting Rabbi Chanina, as in Rif’s reading.[^12] Rabbi Asi reports in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name in [Berakhot 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.2) and Yevamot 28b,[^13] and in his name in Shabbat 25b,[^14] [Chullin 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.98a.17), and [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.3.4.5) and [Nazir 6:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nazir.6.9.6).
Rabbi Asi reports in Rabbi Yannai’s name in Niddah 12a.[^15]

Rabbi Asi also reports in Rabbi Mani’s name in [Kiddushin 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.13a.10), [Bava Batra 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.59b.2), [Chullin 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.21a.11), and [Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kiddushin.1.3.4). The scholar Sh. P. R., in volume 2, page 436, says that this Rabbi Asi who reports in Rabbi Mani’s name is Rabbi Yose bar Bun, and that he was the arranger of the Jerusalem Talmud. All his statements are mistaken. He did not examine all the passages, which concern Rabbi Asi, the colleague of Rabbi Ami. Rabbi Mani is the first sage of that name, who lived in Rabbi Yochanan’s time, as explained in his entry.

He also reports in the name of Rabbi Mana bar Tanchum, as in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 5:4 and Eruvin 6:3. In [Bava Kamma 112b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.112b.4), “Rav Ashi said in Rabbi Shabbetai’s name” should read Rabbi Asi. This is the reading of Rif, Rosh, and Dikdukei Soferim,[^16] and likewise of [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.3.9.23).

His principal teacher, however, before whom he sat throughout his life, was Rabbi Yochanan. Thus, “Rabbi Asi sat before Rabbi Yochanan”[^17] appears in [Pesachim 106a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.106a.11). In [Chullin 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b.20) he told Rabbi Yochanan, “You have taught us, our teacher.” [Shabbat 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.45b.9-10) explicitly calls Rabbi Asi a student of Rabbi Yochanan. In [Chagigah 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.13a.7), Rabbi Elazar said to him, “Rabbi Yochanan, your teacher.” He addressed Rabbi Yochanan as “Master” in [Gittin 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.37a.13) and [Bava Batra 130b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.130b.12), and questioned him in [Gittin 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.74b.7-8), [Kiddushin 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.62a.12), [Bava Metzia 73a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.73a.6), [Avodah Zarah 58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.58b.4-5), and [Meilah 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Meilah.7a.1-6).

Rabbi Asi reports in Rabbi Yochanan’s name in [Shabbat 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.20a.2), [44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.44a.1), [47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.47a.2), and 125a;[^18] [Eruvin 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.12a.10) and [12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.12b.15); [Pesachim 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.24b.7) and 75b; [Yoma 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.24b.11) and [27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.27b.6), followed by the source’s citation “פס:”; [Beitzah 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.35b.13) and [37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.37b.16); [Rosh Hashanah 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.12b.11); [Taanit 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.4b.12) and [29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.29b.5); [Chagigah 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.22b.16); [Moed Katan 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.3b.11), [6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.6a.13), [10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.10a.3), and [13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.13b.4)[^19]; [Yevamot 67b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.67b.8), [82b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.82b.4), and 100b; [Ketubot 85a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.85a.18); [Nedarim 82b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.82b.2); [Gittin 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.23b.1), [50b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.50b.14), and [78b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.78b.10); [Kiddushin 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.13a.12), [39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.39a.6-7), and [60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.60a.4); [Bava Metzia 72b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.72b.10); [Bava Batra 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.3a.6), [8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.8a.15-16), [55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.55a.9), and [84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.84b.7); [Sanhedrin 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.41b.9); [Makkot 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.19b.15); [Avodah Zarah 58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.58b.6); and [Chullin 103b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.103b.10).

Rabbi Yochanan called him one of the youngsters,[^20] as in [Shabbat 145b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.145b.10-11), and he attended to Rabbi Yochanan, as in [Ketubot 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.62a.8). He also recounts practical rulings arising from events that occurred before Rabbi Yochanan, as in [Yevamot 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.65b.13) and 101b.[^21] In the Jerusalem Talmud he reports in Rabbi Yochanan’s name in numerous places.

He was so beloved by his teacher that [Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.9.3.9) tells of a man who came to Rabbi Yochanan and described a dream: he had seen the heavens falling, and one of Rabbi Yochanan’s students supported them so that they did not fall. Rabbi Yochanan passed all his students before the man, who recognized Rabbi Asi.[^22] This is a kind of figurative expression indicating that he was one of his teacher’s foremost students. In Ketubot 17b,[^23] when Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi received ordination, people sang for them, “Ordain for us all who are like these!” He rose so greatly that he became a disciple-colleague of Rabbi Yochanan. In [Yevamot 96b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.96b.14-16), when Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi came to appease Rabbi Yochanan on Rabbi Elazar’s behalf, he grew angry with them and said, “Are you making us colleagues too?” This occurred in their early years before him. In [Meilah 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Meilah.6b.15) we find Rabbi Asi saying to Rabbi Yochanan, “My colleagues in the Diaspora have already taught me.” Rabbi Zeira then called him “my teacher,” and he did not take offense. Such language comes only from a disciple-colleague, not from a student addressing his teacher.
He also reports in Reish Lakish’s name, as in Shabbat 45a[^24] and [63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.63a.28), Chullin 98a, and [Bekhorot 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.25a.13).
In [Yoma 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.43b.4) Rabbi Asi relates how little Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish could derive when they examined the passage of the red heifer.

His colleagues. First and foremost was Rabbi Ami. They studied together, as in [Berakhot 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.8a.20) and [Shabbat 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.10a.5), and received ordination together. Both were called “the priests of the Land of Israel.” They were together even while in Babylonia, and were appointed judges of the Land of Israel together. We always find them together, as I have already discussed at length in Rabbi Ami’s entry.

Rabbi Abba: [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.2.6.2) relates that a case came before Rabbi Ami; Rabbi Abba spoke, and Rabbi Asi said, “Were it not for Rabbi Ba, we would already have been on the point of permitting a married woman.” In [Shabbat 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.45b.9), the two visited the house of Rabbi Abba of Haifa.

Rabbi Abba bar Memel was greater than he. In [Chullin 129a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.129a.2) Rabbi Asi told Rabbi Zeira, “It was difficult for me too, and I asked Rabbi Abba bar Memel,[^25] who told me,” and so forth.
Rabbi Abba bar Zavda was greater than Rabbi Asi. In Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 2:5 and Sanhedrin 1:2, Rabbi Abba bar Zavda opened, while Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, Rabbi Asi, and Rabbi Ami signed.

Rabbi Abbahu, as discussed in Rabbi Ami’s entry: in [Yevamot 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.65b.13), Rabbi Acha bar Chanina reports in Rabbi Abbahu’s name in Rabbi Asi’s name; the reading should be the same there at [101a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.101a.5). Rabbi Asi was undoubtedly[^26] much older than Rabbi Abbahu, but both were students of Rabbi Yochanan.

Rabbi Elazar: although in [Berakhot 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.27b.11) we find Rabbi Asi reporting in Rabbi Elazar’s name—and the same reading is required in [Niddah 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.63a.5), where Rav Ashi is a mistake for Rabbi Asi[^27]—they were colleagues. Thus, [Berakhot 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.16a.3) has Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi arranging his wedding canopy. In Kiddushin Rabbi Elazar addresses Rabbi Asi.

In [Chagigah 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.13a.7) Rabbi Asi said to Rabbi Elazar, “Come, let me teach you the Account of the Chariot.” He replied, “Had I merited it, I would have learned it from Rabbi Yochanan, your teacher.” His saying “your teacher” rather than “our teacher” is explained by Hyman as follows. Rabbi Yochanan taught the Account of the Chariot to Rabbi Asi, whereas Rabbi Elazar declined it, saying, “I am not yet old enough.”

In Chullin 103a[^28] Rabbi Elazar questioned Rabbi Asi. The passage explains that Rabbi Elazar had no need to question Rabbi Asi; rather, Rabbi Asi had forgotten his learning and Rabbi Elazar came to remind him. Rabbi Elazar said, “Exemplar of the generation! Have you not said many times before Rabbi Yochanan,” and so forth. In [Eruvin 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.47a.17) and [Bekhorot 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.3a.19)[^30], Rabbi Elazar did not enter the study hall and encountered Rabbi Asi,[^29] and so forth. Zeiri bar Chama was his host, as in [Yoma 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.78a.9).

Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba: they were always together. In [Eruvin 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65b.19) both arrived at a certain inn, and in [Chullin 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.49a.13) they visited Rabbi Mallukh’s locality. In [Moed Katan 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.10a.3) and [13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.13b.4) both report in the names of Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yochanan. In [Eruvin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.32b.4) they sat together; in Yevamot 25b[^31] Rabbi Asi quoted Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi to him. In [Yoma 73a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.73a.13)[^32] Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba spoke, and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away. [Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 1:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Chagigah.1.7.3) relates that Rabbi Yehudah Nesia sent all three throughout the towns of Israel to arrange teachers for them. In [Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.2.5.2), Rabbi Abba bar Zavda opened, while Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, Rabbi Ami, and Rabbi Asi signed. In [Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.6.4.4), Rabbi Chiyya, Rabbi Ami, and Rabbi Asi went up to Chamat Gader and asked Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef; Rabbi Yochanan heard and said, “You did well.”[^33] [Shabbat 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.32b.4) gives a disagreement between Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Yose. Hyman proposes reading Rabbi Asi for Rabbi Yose. In [Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, at the end of 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.1.1.7), Rabbi Yasa and Rabbi Chiyya bar Va found something written in Rabbi Hillel bar Rabbi Elam’s notebook.[^34]
Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin disagrees with Rabbi Asi in [Sukkah 35a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.35a.7).
Rabbi Chanina, “the colleague of the sages,”[^35] lived in his time, as in [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.16).
Rabbi Chanina bar Yosef disagrees with Rabbi Asi in [Eruvin 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65b.21), but was older than Rabbi Asi.
Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Chanina: in [Bava Kamma 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.42b.7) Rabbi Asi says, “I heard this matter from a great man, namely Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Chanina.”
Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi, as discussed in Rabbi Ami’s entry.
Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha was greater than Rabbi Asi. In [Bava Kamma 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.60b.11) Rabbi Asi sat before him and addressed him as “Master.”[^36]

Rabbi Mallukh: Rabbi Asi, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, and Rabbi Zeira visited him and asked whether he had stated a ruling, and so forth ([Chullin 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.49a.13)). Rabbah bar Rav Natan was his colleague, as in [Eruvin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.32b.4).
Rabbi Sheila of Kefar Temarta: [Megillah 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.16a.1) has Rabbi Asi saying, “Rabbi Sheila expounded,” and so forth.
Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak appears with Rabbi Asi in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, at the end of 2:1. Rabbi Asi reports in his name in [Tamid 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.31b.11).
His students and those who transmitted his teachings. Rabbi Abba bar Bizna reports in his name in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 5:7.
Rabbi Avin: in [Kiddushin 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.44a.15-16) Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Zeira whether Rabbi Avin was reliable.
Rabbi Oshaya questions Rabbi Asi in [Menachot 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.3b.20)[^37] and speaks in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Shabbat 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.18a.8).
Rabbi Acha reports in his name in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:4 and Bikkurim 1:3.

Rabbi Acha bar Avya sat before Rabbi Asi in [Bava Batra 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.56a.5)[^38] and reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Pesachim 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.24b.7) and [Chullin 50b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.50b.3).
Rabbi Acha bar Chanina reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Shabbat 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.45b.10) and [Sanhedrin 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.41b.9)[^39].
Rabbi Achi was in charge of bills of divorce in his time, as in [Gittin 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.5b.20).

Rabbi Ila reports in Rabbi Yasa’s name in [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.1.4.3). [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.15-16)[^40] is Hyman’s evidence for treating Ila as a colleague of Rabbi Asi. Ashyan bar Yakim questioned Rabbi Yasa in [Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.11.7.3)[^41].

Rabbi Bivi reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Shabbat 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.14a.4), [Shevuot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.6b.7), and [Makkot 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.19b.10) and 21b[^42]. Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi visited him, as in [Shabbat 74a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.74a.6).
Bar Hedya wished to bring a bill of divorce and came before Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi ([Gittin 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.5b.20)).

Rabbi Berekhya reports in his name [at the end of Bereshit Rabbah 77](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.77.3). [Eikhah Rabbah 4:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah.4.18)[^43] has Rabbi Chalfo bar Zevid and Rabbi Berekhya reporting in Rabbi Isi’s name. Gamliel Zuga questioned Rabbi Yasa [at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.11.5.10); Hyman identifies this Rabbi Yasa with Rabbi Asi and refers to the beginning of Shabbat, chapter 2.

Rabbi Zeira: when Rabbi Zeira went up to the Land of Israel, he encountered Rabbi Asi, as in [Gittin 74a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.74a.21), Kiddushin 4b[^44], and [Chullin 75b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.75b.6)[^46]. He questioned Rabbi Asi in [Shabbat 71a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.71a.4)[^47] and [130b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.130b.4); in Niddah 54b[^45], too, Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi, “Many times I have asked you,” and so forth. In [Bava Batra 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.84b.8) he said, “Perhaps my teacher has not heard,” and so forth; in [Chullin 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.6a.12) he called him “Master.” In [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.2.5) and [Kiddushin 1:7, at 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kiddushin.1.7.4), Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Yasa, “Does my teacher know Bar Pedaya?”[^48] In [Pesachim 106a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.106a.11)[^49] Rabbi Zeira sat before him, and in [Avodah Zarah 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.16b.12) he transmits a teaching in Rabbi Asi’s name. Yet in [Chullin 107b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.107b.2-3) we find that when Rabbi Zeira went up and encountered Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, he said, “Could two great men such as you err concerning Rav and Shmuel?” In [Avodah Zarah 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.16b.11) Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Asi, “Does the Master not hold,” and so forth, and Rabbi Asi replied, “Black pot! Between you and me the teaching will be completed.” From this we see that Rabbi Zeira was already a leading sage when he came to the Land of Israel. Nevertheless, Rabbi Asi had sat throughout his life before Rabbi Yochanan and had also received teachings from Rabbi Yochanan’s teachers, while Rabbi Zeira had been Rav Yehudah’s student in Babylonia. He was therefore considered Rabbi Asi’s disciple-colleague.
Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda speaks in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Megillah 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.31b.6).
Rabbi Chinena speaks in his name in [Tamid 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.31b.11)[^50].
Rav Chanina Sava reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Pesachim 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.75a.4)[^51].

Rav Yehudah bar Sheila reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name in [Shabbat 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.44a.1), [126a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.126a.6), and [142b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.142b.14)[^52]; [Yevamot 82b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.82b.4); and [Zevachim 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.22a.12). In [Niddah 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.63a.5), where Rav Yehudah bar Sheila reports in Rav Ashi’s name in Rabbi Elazar’s name, Hyman proposes reading Rabbi Asi.
Rav Yehudah bar Shmuel reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in Yevamot 82b[^53].
[Taanit 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.12b.7) has Rav Yehoshua, the son of Rav Idi, visiting Rabbi Asi’s house, but Hyman takes this to be a scribal error for Rav Ashi’s house.
Rav Yosef reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Shabbat 125b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.125b.3).
Rabbi Yaakov reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Kiddushin 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.13a.10).

Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha (1) reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Taanit 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.27b.3), [Moed Katan 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.27a.15), [Zevachim 116b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.116b.4), and at [the end of the proems to Eikhah Rabbah, proem 33](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah%2C_Petichta.33).

Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi questions Rabbi Yose in [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.5.4.5-6) and raises an objection before him at the beginning of [Berakhot 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.6.3).
Rabbi Yaakov, son of Rabbi Sosai, appears before Rabbi Yose at the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.4.9.2).
Rabbi Yaakov of the South speaks before Rabbi Yasa in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:5[^54] and reports in his name in Maaser Sheni 3:4[^55] and at the beginning of Yevamot, chapter 1, at 3a[^60].
Rabbi Yirmeyah questions Rabbi Asi in [Gittin 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.44a.19) and [Chullin 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.21a.12).

In [Kiddushin 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.60a.4) Rav Mesharshiya, the son of Rav Ami, says to Rabbi Asi, “I shall explain it to you”; it appears that the order should be reversed[^56]. Nechemya, the son-in-law of the patriarchal household, says, “I saw Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi reach a stream of water,” and so forth ([Yoma 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.78a.3)).

Rav Nachman: [Eruvin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.32b.4) is quoted as saying, “Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Asi bar Rav Natan were sitting, and Rav Nachman sat with them.” It is known that when Rabbi Asi was in the Land of Israel, Rav Nachman had either not yet been born or was still a small child. Rabbi Asi had gone up to the Land of Israel in Rav’s lifetime, since he still received teachings from Rabbi Chanina, as explained above, and Rav Nachman was not in the Land of Israel. It is therefore impossible to say, as the author of Dorot ha-Rishonim does in volume 2, page 239, note קבב, that this occurred before Rabbi Asi went up to the Land of Israel.

It is very plausible, however, that Rabbi Asi returned briefly to Babylonia, like his colleagues Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Elazar, and that they sat together then. We likewise find in [Shabbat 119a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.119a.4)[^57] that Rav Nachman—the words “bar Yitzchak” are a scribal error—said, “If Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi happened to come, would we not,” and so forth. The wording implies that he knew them. More likely still, the reading should be “Rav Nachman bar Kohen sat with them,” and the event occurred in the Land of Israel, for Rav Nachman bar Kohen was a Jerusalemite, as in [Ketubot 105b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.105b.2)[^58]. Similarly, Chullin 8b[^59] has Rav Nachman bar Kohen, according to the reading of Shittah Mekubbetzet and Dikdukei Soferim, reporting in Rabbi Asi’s name: “I saw Rabbi Yochanan eat meat slaughtered by a Samaritan.” Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Chullin 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.5b.9).
Rabbi Simon reports in his name in [Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.1.6.2)[^61].

Rav Avira gives teachings in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Berakhot 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.20b.15), [Pesachim 119b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.119b.4), [Gittin 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.7a.18-20), [Sotah 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.4b.4), and [Chullin 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.84b.4)[^62].
Rabbi Pedat, Rabbi Elazar’s son, was his public interpreter, as explicitly stated at the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.4.10.5).

Rabbi Pinchas reports in Rabbi Asi’s name [at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.11.2.8). Rabbah, the son of Rabbah bar Rav Huna, reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Chullin 76a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.76a.12-13)[^63]. Rabbah reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Shabbat 135a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.135a.11-13)[^64] and, according to the reading of Dikdukei Soferim, in Chullin 76a.[^65] Rabbah bar bar Chana said, “I was standing before Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi” ([Chullin 106a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.106a.15)).
Rabbi Shabbetai and Rabbi Chasida brought a case before Rabbi Yasa at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Nazir, chapter 2. Rabbi Yasa ruled for Shemuta bar Rabbi Chanina in Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:8.
Rabbi Tanchum reports in Rabbi Asi’s name in [Berakhot 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.2).

Rabbi Tanchum bar Mari reports in his name in [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 8:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.8.10.3)[^66]. Of his personal activities we find that his occupation was making linen garments, as evident in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 3:3. He was also eager to learn about nature. [Vayikra Rabbah, at the beginning of chapter 19](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.19.1), relates that he took young ravens, put them in a pot, and closed it for three days. When he opened it, he found that gnats had been generated from their droppings, and these sustained them. He applied to them the verse, “Who prepares food for the raven?”

[Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.9.3.9)[^67] relates that Rabbi Asi fasted for eighty days in order to see Rabbi Chiyya the Great. In the end he saw him, and his eyes grew dim.

The alternative account in [Shabbat 119a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.119a.4) relates that he and Rabbi Ami shouldered loads and brought them in to honor Shabbat. We have already explained at length in Rabbi Ami’s entry that the two were equal in wisdom, both were judges of the Land of Israel, and after Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar died they were the generation’s leading sages. We do find that Rabbi Asi had a public interpreter to proclaim his teachings to the people: Jerusalem Talmud Megillah, at the end of 4:10, states that Rabbi Pedat was his interpreter. Rabbi Asi, however, did not wish to accept the burden of leadership, as related in the old Tanchuma, Mishpatim. At the time of his death he regretted this and wept.
Accordingly, the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4, states that after Rabbi Yochanan, Rabbi Ami became head of the academy, without mentioning Rabbi Asi.

Apparently Rabbi Asi died before Rabbi Ami. We find that Rabbi Asi died in Tiberias: [Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.3.1.13)[^68] relates, “When Rabbi Yasa died, the castle of Tiberias fell.” Rabbi Ami, however, went with his academy to Caesarea toward the end of his life, under Rabbi Abbahu’s protection, while Rabbi Yehudah Nesia II remained in Tiberias. This is the meaning of [Rosh Hashanah 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.20a.17), where Rabbi Yehudah Nesia sent Rabbi Ami the message, “Know that throughout Rabbi Yochanan’s life he used to teach us,” and so forth. Likewise, [Beitzah 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.27a.4) relates that Rabbi Yehudah Nesia sent that firstborn animal before Rabbi Ami; Rabbi Asi is not mentioned there.

His death is also mentioned in [Moed Katan 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25b.13): when Rabbi Asi died, all the trees were uprooted. [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1, at 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.3.1.12), relates that Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba accepted mourning when Rabbi Yasa died, yet ate meat and drank wine, since he did not observe the preburial restrictions of aninut. Perhaps this was because Rabbi Asi was his colleague; in [Moed Katan 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25b.11) Chiyya bar Abba says in Rabbi Yochanan’s name that even for a teacher who taught one wisdom, one sits in mourning for only one day. Accordingly, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba ruled that shoes could be worn that very day, as in [Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.7.16). After Rabbi Asi’s death, the sages came to collect his teachings, as in [Kiddushin 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.13a.10).[^11]

notes.text: Hyman’s interval of several years between Asi’s arrival and the episode involving his mother is his chronological reconstruction. Kiddushin 31b relates the episode without specifying that interval.
The additional Yoma reference פס: is unclear in the supplied Hebrew and has been left unexpanded.

In the supplied quotation from Eruvin 32b, אסי בר רב נתן runs the names together. The consulted Talmud text lists Rabbi Asi and Rava bar Natan separately. Hyman elsewhere calls the latter Rabbah bar Rav Natan; his proposed changes involving Rav Nachman are retained as his arguments.
The supplied text has בו סוסיי. Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4:9 reads ברבי סוסיי, “son of Rabbi Sosai.”

The supplied פנחם has been rendered Pinchas, as in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:2. In the consulted edition, the Hebrew attributes his report to Rabbi Yose, while its English translation reads Rabbi Yasa; Hyman identifies the source as Rabbi Asi.
Hyman first cites the passage about Rabbi Pedat as Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:4 and later as 4:10. The passage is found at 4:10 in the consulted edition.

Hyman describes Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba as mourning and himself eating meat and drinking wine. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1 instead says that he received Asi’s mourners and served them meat and wine. Moed Katan 3:7 explicitly records his permission to wear shoes on the day Asi died.

Hyman’s identifications, chronological reconstructions, and proposed reversals or emendations of transmission chains are preserved as his arguments. Readings attributed to Rif, Rosh, Dikdukei Soferim, and other works are presented on his authority.

For Hyman’s other similarly named sages, see [Rav Asi](https://www.girsology.com/toledot?entry=h-9022ca7e706930d3&lang=en) and [Rav Athi (Ithi), colleague of Rav Ashi](https://www.girsology.com/toledot?entry=h-d5d9554b20b20d28&lang=en).

Meilah 6b–7a contains Asi’s statement about “my colleagues in the Diaspora” and Rabbi Zeira’s reply, “You have already taught us.” Hyman’s conclusion about their status as disciple-colleagues is his interpretation of these exchanges.

The linked Kiddushin passages give the mother episode and the collection of Asi’s teachings after his death. Eruvin lists Rabbi Asi and Rava bar Natan separately. The two Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot passages concern the mother and the feeding of mourners respectively. The consulted Megillah identifies Pedat as Asi’s interpreter and Moed Katan gives the shoe ruling after his death.

In the consulted Bavli, Rabbi Zeira cites Rabbi Chanina, who cites Rav Ashi in Rabbi’s name. The consulted [Rif Gittin 21a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Gittin.21a.2) reads Rabbi Zeira citing Rabbi Asi, who cites Rabbi Chanina in Rabbi’s name.

At Berakhot 29b the consulted Bavli reads Rav Asi, while [Rif Berakhot 20a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Berakhot.20a.2) reads Rabbi Asi. [Yevamot 75b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.75b.11) gives a Rabbi Asi transmission from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Hyman’s 28b locator remains unconfirmed.

The cited Shabbat locator remains unconfirmed. In the linked Jerusalem Talmud Nazir passage, the Hebrew names Yasa and Yehoshua ben Levi together in Bar Pedaiah’s name, while the accompanying English renders a chain through Yehoshua ben Levi.
The cited Asi-to-Yannai attribution remains unconfirmed in the consulted text at this locator.
The consulted Bavli reads Rav Ashi. The linked Jerusalem Talmud Hebrew has Rabbi Yose in Rabbi Shabbetai’s name, and Guggenheimer’s note proposes Yasa, citing Dikdukei Soferim.
The consulted passage first puts Rabbi Zeira before Rav Asi. A second version puts Rav Asi before Rabbi Yochanan, as in Hyman’s example.

The Asi transmission listed as Pesachim 75b appears at [Pesachim 75a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.75a.4) in the consulted text. The listed Shabbat 125a and Yevamot 100b transmissions remain unconfirmed.

In both cited Moed Katan passages, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Asi report in the names of Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yochanan. The individual rulings are left unassigned. Beitzah 35b gives the transmission through Rabbi Yochanan as an alternate version.
Rabbi Yochanan addresses both Rabbi Asi and Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba as “youngsters.”
The practical incident at the cited Yevamot 101b locator remains unconfirmed.
The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Hebrew names Rabbi Yose as the student recognized in the dream. The accompanying translation gives Assi and explains that identification in a note.
The ordination song appears at [Ketubot 17a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.17a.3) in the consulted text. Hyman cites 17b.

The candelabrum report is at [Shabbat 45b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.45b.10) in the consulted text. The linked Shabbat 63a gives Asi as an alternate transmitter. At [Chullin 98a:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.98a.17), Rav Asi cites Yehoshua ben Levi in bar Kappara’s name. The Reish Lakish attribution at that locator remains unconfirmed. The cited Bekhorot passage reads Rav Ashi.

The exchange begins at [Chullin 128b:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.128b.22). At 129a the Hebrew says “he said to him.” The accompanying English takes Rabbi Zeira as the speaker here, while Hyman takes Rabbi Asi as the speaker.

In the cited Yevamot 101a Hebrew, Acha bar Chanina cites Abaye, who cites Asi in Yochanan’s name. The accompanying English omits Asi. Hyman proposes the Abbahu reading on the basis of the earlier passage.
The consulted Niddah text reads Rav Ashi. Rabbi Asi is Hyman’s proposed reading.
The question and reminder appear at [Chullin 103b:11-14](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.103b.11-14) in the consulted text. Hyman cites 103a.
In the consulted text Eruvin names Rabbi Eliezer, while Bekhorot names Rabbi Elazar.
The Bekhorot exchange continues at [Bekhorot 3b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.3b.1).
Hyman cites 25b. The exchange in which Rabbi Asi quotes Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba appears at [Yevamot 75b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.75b.11) in the consulted text.
The passage names Rabbi Abbahu as the speaker and gives Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba as the alternative. Ami and Asi turn away in both accounts.
The consulted Rosh Hashanah text gives Chiyya without a patronymic. The consulted Eruvin text names Chama bar Yosef, where Hyman writes Chiyya bar Yosef.

The consulted Hebrew says Rabbi Yose reported the notebook finding in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Va, and calls its owner Rabbi Hillel ben Rabbi Ales. The accompanying English renders the patronymics as bar Abba and ben Rabbi Vales.
The linked funeral account names Rabbi Chanina among the contemporaries and leaves the epithet unstated.
The passage has both Ami and Asi sitting before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha and leaves their individual requests unnamed.
The question is attributed to Rav Hoshaya. An alternate report has him address it to Rabbi Asi. The question continues at [Menachot 4a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.4a.1).
Rabbi Asi is the person before whom Rav Acha sits in this passage. The source he cites there is named Rabbi Asi bar Chanina.

In both passages Acha bar Chanina speaks in Asi’s name. The consulted Sanhedrin text uses “Rabbi Asi” here and “Rav Asi” in the second transmission at [Sanhedrin 41b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.41b.12).
The passage gives two accounts of whether Ila went out to meet Rav Huna’s coffin. It leaves the relationship between Ila and Asi unstated.
The consulted Hebrew names the sage whom Ashyan questions as Yasa. The accompanying English calls him Yose.
The consulted [Makkot 21b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.21b.3) reads “Rav Bivi said in the name of Rabbi Yosei,” whereas the three preceding linked passages have Rav Bivi citing Rav Asi.
The consulted wording names Berekhya and Chalafi bar Zevid as speaking in Isi’s name. The same passage also names an Asi of Caesarea earlier.
Hyman supplies this locator. The consulted 4b concerns betrothal and does not confirm the encounter, which the linked Gittin and Chullin passages relate.
The exchange Hyman quotes appears in the consulted edition at [Niddah 53b:11-14](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.53b.11-14), where Zeira recalls asking several times and receiving no reply.
The Hebrew has Zeira arrive and find Asi, as in Hyman’s account. The accompanying English has Asi find Zeira.
The passage gives two versions of the question: Zeira asks Asi, or Yirmeya asks Zeira.
In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat text, Yasa says he received the teaching through Yochanan. The Kiddushin parallel instead names Rav Adda bar Achava.
The passage gives two versions: Zeira sat before Asi, or Asi sat before Yochanan.
The consulted text calls the speaker Rav Chinena. He cites Asi, who cites Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak.
Rav Chinena bar Idi is the questioner. The teaching he quotes runs from Rav Chinena the Elder through Rabbi Asi to Rabbi Yochanan.
In this account, Yehudah bar Sheila quotes Asi telling how the group put the question to Yochanan. The adjacent references give the chain explicitly.
Hyman supplies this reference for Yehudah bar Shmuel. The consulted [Yevamot 82b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.82b.4) names Yehudah bar Sheila, who cites Asi citing Yochanan.
The consulted [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.10.5.2) names Yehoshua the Southerner speaking before Yasa. Guggenheimer prefers the reading Yose.

The consulted [Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 3:5:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.3.5.6) has Yaakov the Southerner asking Rabbi Yose a question. That passage has a different chapter subdivision and a different attribution from the one Hyman reports.
The consulted passage gives Mesharshiya speaking to Asi. The proposed reversal is Hyman’s.
The consulted text includes “bar Yitzchak.” In its alternative account Ami and Asi speak of how they would receive Yochanan.
Rav Dimi reports a teaching by Rav Nachman bar Kohen. The passage itself does not name Jerusalem or identify the participant in the earlier Eruvin scene.

Hyman supplies 8b and attributes the reading bar Kohen to Shittah Mekubbetzet and Dikdukei Soferim. The directly consulted [Chullin 5b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.5b.9) has the testimony about Yochanan eating Samaritan slaughter, with bar Yitzchak as Asi’s transmitter. Hyman’s witnesses for bar Kohen have not been collated here.
In the consulted [Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 1:6:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.1.6.2), Yaakov the Southerner speaks before Rabbi Yose, where Hyman says he reports in Yasa’s name.
The consulted passage has Rabbi Simon quoting Rabbi Yose, who cites Nehorai.
Each of the linked passages reports that Avira sometimes attributed the teaching to Ami and sometimes to Asi. Gittin gives this alternating attribution for two separate teachings.
The consulted text names Rava son of Rabbah bar Rav Huna in the transmission through Asi. In the preceding two transmissions, Rabbah and Rabbah bar Rav Huna cite Ashi.
The consulted text gives the statement directly from Rabbi Asi and has Abaye question him. Asi’s reply continues at [Shabbat 135b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.135b.1).
The separate attribution to Rabbah rests on Hyman’s report of the Dikdukei Soferim reading.
The consulted Hebrew and English name Rabbi Yose in Tanchum bar Mari’s transmission.
Hyman and Guggenheimer’s English give eighty days and name Asi. The consulted Hebrew reads Rabbi Yose and “eight days.”
The Hebrew names Rabbi Yasa and says the kistolin of Tiberias fell. Hyman has “castle,” while Guggenheimer interprets it as a sacred fountain.
